headline: Soviet fighter shoots down Korean Air Lines Flight 007
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 1 September 1983 listed under Northeast Asia a South Korean airliner "reported missing," Soviet denials (via KYODO) that it had landed on Sakhalin or was in Soviet territory, and an item that Soviet air space had been "violated."

headline: Reagan proposes his Middle East peace plan
fbis: The Middle East & Africa contents for September 1982 listed reaction to the Reagan initiative: Israeli items from Peres, Begin's office and West Bank figures, an Algerian commentary on Reagan's "pacification plan," JANA on his TV speech, and Tunisia's Es-Sebsi calling it progress.

headline: United States recognizes Baltic independence
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 3 September 1991 carried Moscow BALTFAX on Bush announcing US recognition of Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian independence after phoning their leaders, followed by TASS on John Major's toast to Baltic independence.

headline: Dnestr region proclaims a separate republic in Moldova
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 4 September 1990 carried TASS reports from Kishinev on Moldova's emergency Supreme Soviet session, called over the Gagauz declaration and a congress of left-bank Dnestr deputies setting up another republic, and its vote to institute presidential rule.

headline: Yeltsin and Kravchuk meet at Massandra over the Black Sea Fleet
fbis: The Central Eurasia Daily Report of 3 September 1993 carried ITAR-TASS on Yeltsin's arrival in Simferopol for talks with Kravchuk at Massandra, and Radio Rossii reporting the Black Sea Fleet, fuel deliveries and payments on the agenda.

headline: Jiang Zemin and Yeltsin sign a joint declaration in Moscow
fbis: The Central Eurasia Daily Report of 6 September 1994 carried, inside an ITAR-TASS press review, ROSSIYSKIYE VESTI on Jiang Zemin's return to Moscow after 40 years as head of China, and Yeltsin on expanding bilateral cooperation; the joint declaration is not described.

headline: Mathias Rust sentenced for his Red Square landing
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 4 September 1987 carried Radio Moscow on the prosecutor asking eight years for Mathias Rust, and DPA reports of Rust's plea for leniency, saying "I made a great mistake," with the verdict expected that afternoon.

headline: Hijackers storm Pan Am Flight 73 at Karachi
fbis: The Middle East review in the Daily Report of 5 September 1986 led with the Pan Am hijacking at Karachi: AFP on a "Libyan Revolutionary Cells" claim, Delhi radio on gunmen in security uniforms killing an Indian crew member, and Karachi radio on demands to fly to Larnaca.

headline: Gunmen massacre worshippers at Istanbul's Neve Shalom synagogue
fbis: The Middle East review in the Daily Report of 8 September 1986 carried Ankara radio reporting 24 killed in the attack on Jews praying at an Istanbul synagogue, Peres vowing to "cut off these murderers," and competing claims including one for Abu Nidal.

headline: Pinochet survives an ambush on his motorcade
fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of 8 September 1986 listed under Chile the attack on Pinochet: an official report, Pinochet's own description, US-made weapons, a toll of seven, the state of siege, and FPMR claims and denials.

headline: Martial law and 'Black Friday' shootings in Tehran
fbis: The Middle East & North Africa Daily Report of 8 September 1978 carried, in badly broken OCR, Tehran radio's announcement of six months' martial law in Tehran from 0600 Friday under General Oveysi, and a report of clashes near Zhaleh Square in which people were killed and wounded.

headline: Bush and Gorbachev meet in Helsinki on the Gulf crisis
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 10 September 1990 carried a TASS report from PRAVDA on Gorbachev's arrival in Helsinki and Bush's arrival statement, hoping to strengthen a common approach to Iraq's "unjustifiable aggression" and speaking of a new world order.

headline: Tajikistan declares independence
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 10 September 1991 carried a commentary on post-coup unrest across the republics, noting that crowds in Dushanbe had removed Tajik President Makhkamov; Tajikistan's independence declaration is not mentioned.
doubt: Page mentions Makhkamov's ouster, not the independence declaration

headline: Hungary opens its border to East German refugees
fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of 11 September 1989 carried Budapest radio on East Germans at the Zanka camp told they could leave, a report that thousands would depart before midnight, and Budapest MTI's government statement on the GDR citizens wishing to resettle in West Germany.

headline: Gorbachev announces withdrawal of the Soviet brigade from Cuba
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 12 September 1991 carried TASS on the Gorbachev-Baker news conference, where Gorbachev said talks with Havana on withdrawing the Soviet training brigade of 11,000 troops would begin soon, and Baker welcomed the decision.

headline: Bush's 'new world order' address to Congress
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 13 September 1990 carried IZVESTIYA's report of Bush's address to Congress, quoting his "new partnership of nations" and a new world where right replaces "the law of the jungle," and his account of the Gulf blockade.

headline: Britain expels 25 Soviet officials after Gordievskiy's defection
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 13 September 1985 carried the London Press Association's report of the Soviet embassy calling Britain's expulsion of 25 officials "an unwarranted action of unfriendly character," based on the allegations of a defector granted asylum.

headline: Turkish military coup
fbis: The South Asia volume's Daily Report of 12 September 1980 led its review with Ankara radio's eight communiques from General Evren's National Security Council: parliament and government "abolished," nationwide martial law, borders closed, and party leaders placed under military custody.

headline: Two-plus-Four Treaty signed in Moscow
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 12 September 1990 carried a TASS report from PRAVDA on Shevardnadze's talks with Baker, who had come to Moscow for the six-power meeting on the German settlement; the discussion centered on the Gulf crisis and the CSCE summit, and the signing itself is not on the page.

headline: Israel and the PLO sign the Oslo Declaration of Principles
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 15 September 1993 carried an interview with Sa'ib Urayqat, who called direct PLO-Israel talks historic but judged the autonomy agreement "far too vague," warning that real negotiations would begin only after the Washington signing.

headline: Lebanon's President-elect Bashir Gemayel assassinated
fbis: The Middle East review in the Daily Report of 15 September 1982 led with Beirut radio's announcement that President-elect Bashir al-Jumayyil had been killed by a bomb at Phalangist headquarters in al-Ashrafiyah, after first reports that he had emerged safely, and the IDF moving into West Beirut.

headline: Rev. Benjamin Weir freed in Lebanon
fbis: The Daily Report of 16 September 1985 (South Asia volume) noted in its regional review that Radio Monte Carlo reported an Islamic Jihad spokesman announcing the release of Benjamin Weir, one of seven Americans kidnapped in Beirut.

headline: Israeli forces enter West Beirut
fbis: The Middle East review in the Daily Report of 15 September 1982 carried IDF radio's statement that Israeli forces had entered West Beirut "to guarantee calm," leftist radio claims of armed resistance, and Prime Minister al-Wazzan calling the move "unjustified."

headline: Sabra and Shatila massacre begins
fbis: The Middle East review in the Daily Report of 17 September 1982 reported clashes and mass arrests in newly occupied West Beirut, Eytan saying the IDF would not enter the camps, and IDF radio announcing it would entrust "purging" Sabra and Shatila to the Phalangists.

headline: Taraki ousted; Hafizullah Amin takes power in Kabul
fbis: The Middle East & North Africa Daily Report of 17 September 1979 listed under Afghanistan Amin meeting the Soviet ambassador on 15 September, Kabul reporting the burial of a Taraki aide, and rebel successes in Herat and Konar.

headline: Camp David Accords signed
fbis: The Middle East & North Africa Daily Report of 18 September 1978 carried, in largely illegible OCR, remarks at the Camp David signing ceremony and a Cairo MENA report that Sadat and Begin, with Carter as witness, had signed a framework for Middle East peace and one for an Egypt-Israel treaty.

headline: Carter mission reaches agreement with Cedras in Haiti
fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of 19 September 1994 carried Colombian television on Carter, Powell and Nunn arriving in Port-au-Prince amid predictions that talks with Cedras would fail, and a report that Castro would send troops to repel invasion; no agreement is reported.
doubt: Page shows the Carter mission arriving, not its agreement

headline: Burmese army seizes power
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 19 September 1988 carried Moscow TASS in English relaying Burmese radio's announcement of a military coup led by General Saw Maung, whose group promised to ease hardships and then hold general elections.

headline: US troops land in Haiti
fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of 19 September 1994 carried items from before the landing: Colombian television on the Carter mission and US sources saying the multinational force would occupy Haiti regardless, and Havana PRENSA LATINA on Clinton's speech justifying the invasion.
doubt: Page predates the landing; it covers the run-up only

headline: Earthquake devastates Mexico City
fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of 20 September 1985 listed under Mexico the earthquake with an estimated 3,000 dead, reports of US diplomats killed, the president's comments, damage in Acapulco, and continuing tremors.

headline: Car bomb hits the US embassy annex in East Beirut
fbis: The Middle East review in the Daily Report of 20 September 1984 led with Beirut radio on a booby-trapped vehicle exploding near the US embassy in Awkar, killing at least 40 and injuring the US and British ambassadors, and an Islamic Jihad claim to AFP.

headline: Yeltsin's Decree 1400 dissolves the Russian parliament
fbis: The supplement on Russia's presidential-parliamentary crisis of 23 September 1993 carried Rutskoy's declaration that he had become acting president and was repealing "anticonstitutional and illegal Edict No. 1400," and his edict overruling Yeltsin from ROSSIYSKAYA GAZETA.

headline: Armenians vote for independence in a referendum
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 23 September 1991 carried a TASS review of PRAVDA, whose Yerevan correspondent reported that 95 percent of voters in the 21 September referendum backed Armenia becoming an independent democratic state outside the Soviet Union, while Ter-Petrosyan promised to join an economic treaty.

headline: Iraq invades Iran
fbis: The Middle East & Africa Daily Report of 22 September 1980 reviewed escalating Shatt al-Arab fighting: INA on Iraq's threats to enforce its navigation rules by force and raids on Abadan airport and Khorramshahr, Tehran radio on "intense" border clashes; the full-scale invasion is not yet reported.
doubt: Page reports border fighting before the invasion, not the invasion itself

headline: Armenia declares independence
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 23 September 1991 carried a TASS review of PRAVDA reporting the 21 September referendum, with 95 percent voting for independence outside the USSR; the parliament's formal declaration is not on the page.
doubt: Page reports the referendum result, not the formal declaration

headline: British hostage Jack Mann freed in Lebanon
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 24 September 1991 carried Beirut radio and the clandestine Voice of the Oppressed on the Revolutionary Justice Organization promising to free Jack Mann within 48 hours thanks to UN efforts, and Tehran IRNA expecting his release "by midnight."

headline: Three Israelis killed aboard a yacht in Larnaca
fbis: The Middle East review in the Daily Report of 25 September 1985 led with Nicosia radio reporting that two Palestinian gunmen had seized an Israeli yacht in Larnaca marina, killing a woman and holding two men hostage, with the PLO office denying any connection.

headline: Vietnam completes its withdrawal from Cambodia
fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of 26 September 1989 carried East Berlin ADN on the GDR Foreign Ministry spokesman welcoming the complete withdrawal of Vietnamese "volunteer units" from Cambodia as a step toward a political solution, stressing prevention of a Pol Pot return.

headline: Bush announces sweeping cuts in tactical nuclear weapons
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 30 September 1991 carried Soviet welcome for Bush's initiative: INTERFAX on Gorbachev's positive televised response, Radio Rossii on Yeltsin's call with Bush urging substantial Soviet reciprocal measures, and TASS on Pankin pledging full support.

headline: Abkhaz forces capture Sukhumi
fbis: The Central Eurasia Daily Report of 27 September 1993 carried Moscow ITAR-TASS on Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Pastukhov calling the downing of civilian airliners "barbaric" and sending Black Sea Fleet landing craft to Sukhumi for refugees; the city's capture is not reported.
doubt: Page covers the fighting around Sukhumi before its capture

headline: Oslo II interim agreement signed in Washington
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 28 September 1995 carried an interview in which Arafat said that for the first time the Palestinian authority would control the whole populated West Bank, and proposed Jerusalem as "capital for two peoples."

headline: Pope John Paul I dies after 33 days
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 29 September 1978 listed under West Europe & Canada a TASS report of the death of Pope John Paul in the Vatican.

headline: The ferry Estonia sinks in the Baltic
fbis: The Central Eurasia Daily Report of 28 September 1994 listed under Estonia a Baltic News Service item that the president had declared a day of mourning over the ferry accident.

headline: Daniloff freed and leaves Moscow
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 29 September 1986 listed under United States & Canada a run of Soviet commentary giving Daniloff and arms "top priority" before the summit, including PRAVDA on Daniloff; his release is not reported.
doubt: Page lists commentary on the Daniloff case, not his release

headline: Military coup overthrows Haiti's President Aristide
fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of 30 September 1991 carried Havana's Radio Rebelde and Radio Reloj on gunfire outside Aristide's residence, soldiers seizing the state radio director after he reported a possible coup, and Aristide's whereabouts unknown.

headline: Zakharov freed in the Daniloff exchange
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 1 October 1986 carried three TASS flashes of 30 September: Reagan and Gorbachev to meet in Reykjavik on 11-12 October, Zakharov released and returning home, and Daniloff "expelled" on 29 September.
